items.q: Beta haemolytic chains that are bacitracin sensitive and PYR positive are identified as what?
items.exp: Bacitracin with PYR marks group A while agalactiae resists bacitracin (CAMP positive); pneumococcus alpha haemolyses with optochin sensitivity. Group A drives rheumatic sequelae.

items.q: Migratory polyarthritis with carditis 3 weeks after sore throat with high ASO needs which long term plan?
o: Secondary penicillin prophylaxis for years against rheumatic recurrence
items.exp: Each streptococcal reprise rekindles valvulitis scarring mitral valves; benzathine schedules by cardiac residue outlast symptoms. Glomerulonephritis instead never recurs rheumatically.
items.kp: Post streptococcal carditis: prophylax for years.

items.q: Smoky urine with periorbital oedema, hypertension and low C3 after impetigo is which entity?
items.exp: Nephritogenic M types seed subepithelial humps consuming complement; pressure and oedema settle with diuresis while antibiotics only truncate spread. Normal C3 with synpharyngitic haematuria is IgA disease.
items.kp: Impetigo then smoky low C3 urine: PSGN.

items.q: Sandpaper rash with strawberry tongue and Pastia lines after pharyngitis is what and treated how?
items.exp: Erythrogenic toxin lysogenised strains rash toxigenically while penicillin eradicates carriage preventing rheumatic sequel; desquamation follows defervescence. Kawasaki spares pharynx with coronary threat.

items.q: Lancet diplococci with draughtsman colonies that are optochin sensitive and bile soluble indicate what?
items.exp: Optochin with bile lysis and quellung swelling triangulate pneumococcus; viridans resist optochin while group A beta haemolyses. Capsule explains invasive potential.
r: Incorrect. Neisseria are diplococci oxidase positive.

items.q: Rusty sputum lobar consolidation in an alcoholic with gram positive diplococci needs which empiric cover?
o: Beta lactam plus macrolide for pneumococcal pneumonia
items.exp: Pneumococcus dominates lobar patterns with bacteraemia risk; dual cover handles atypical coinfection while cultures and urinary antigen confirm. TB cavitates upper lobes chronically.
items.kp: Rusty lobar sputum: cover pneumococcus plus atypicals.

items.q: Pneumococcal meningitis with possible penicillin resistance is treated empirically how?
items.exp: Mosaic PBP resistance survives penicillin behind blood brain barrier; dual bactericidal cover with dexamethasone precedes tailoring. Viral patterns show lymphocytic calm.
r: Incorrect. No vesicles or temporal signs.
items.kp: Meningitic diplococci: double cover the barrier.

items.q: A 38 week mother with unknown GBS status in labour needs what to protect the neonate?
o: Intrapartum penicillin against early onset GBS sepsis
items.exp: Vertical transmission seeds early sepsis within days; intrapartum dosing sterilises the canal while screening at 35 to 37 weeks stratifies. Late onset meningitis escapes this net.
r: Incorrect. No neonatal GBS vaccine exists.
items.kp: Unknown GBS in labour: dose penicillin now.

items.q: Subacute fever with Osler nodes and Roth spots weeks after dental work in mitral prolapse suggests what?
items.exp: Dextran sticky viridans lodge on jet lesions growing indolent vegetations with immune phenomena; prolonged penicillin with gentamicin synergy cures while cultures confirm. Aureus destroys acutely.
items.kp: Dental work then immune spots: viridans valve.

items.q: UTI growing enterococci resistant to cephalosporins with vanA positivity is managed how?
o: Ampicillin if sensitive else linezolid or daptomycin with source control
items.exp: Intrinsic cephalosporin resistance makes cephalosporins futile; ampicillin suits sensitive strains while VRE needs oxazolidinone or lipopeptide (off lung). Catheter removal shortens courses.
items.kp: Cephalosporin proof UTI cocci: think enterococcus.
